title: The S3 XGA accelerator registers
covers: The enhanced-mode registers of S3's graphics accelerators, reached in memory from hex 0000 to hex EFFF: the drawing and streams processor registers of the Trio32, Trio64 and Trio64V+, and the S3 ViRGE's engine, command DMA, color pattern and status registers, as DOSBox-X maps them, and the I/O ports 42E8H, 46E8H, 4AE8H and 82E9H, and the further ports 86E9H, 8EE9H, 92E9H, 96E9H, 9EE8H, 9EE9H, A6E9H, AAE9H, AEE9H, B2E9H, BAE9H, BEE9H, E2E0H and E2EAH.

rows.text: Table 13-1 lists hex 8100 and 8102 as the packed MMIO addresses of the current Y and current X registers, ALT CURXY.
A write stores the current Y position, the vertical coordinate where the first pixel is drawn.
A dword write carries the y value in the low word and the x value in the high word.
Bits 11-0 are the current vertical position.
A write stores the current X position, the horizontal coordinate where the first pixel is drawn.
Bits 11-0 are the current horizontal position.
Hex 8104 and 8106 are the addresses of the second current Y and second current X registers.
A write stores the second current Y position, the starting vertical position of a polygon's second edge.
Bits 11-0 are the second vertical position.
DOSBox-X also stores the high word of a dword write to 8104 as the second horizontal position.
A write to 8106 stores the second current X position, the starting horizontal position of a polygon's second edge.
A write to 8106 stores bits 11-0 as the second horizontal position.
Hex 8108 and 810A are the addresses of the destination vertical and horizontal position registers.
A write stores the destination vertical position: the top of the destination rectangle, a line's ending position or its axial step constant.
A write stores the destination horizontal position: the left side of the destination rectangle, a line's ending position or its diagonal step constant.
Bits 11-0 are the destination vertical position and the destination horizontal position.
Bits 13-0 are the line's axial step constant and its diagonal step constant.
DOSBox-X also stores the high word of a dword write to 8108 as the destination horizontal position.
Hex 810C and 810E are the addresses of the second destination vertical and horizontal position registers.
A write stores the second destination vertical position, the ending position of a polygon's second edge or its axial step constant 2.
Bits 11-0 are the second vertical position.
DOSBox-X also stores the high word of a dword write to 810C as the second horizontal position.
A write to 810E stores the second destination horizontal position, the ending position of a polygon's second edge or its diagonal step constant 2.
A write to 810E stores bits 11-0 as the second horizontal position.
Hex 8110 is the address of the line error term register.
A write stores the initial error term of a solid or textured line draw.
Bits 13-0 are the line parameter or error term.
Hex 8120 is the address of the background color register.
Bits 31-0 are the background color.
DOSBox-X keeps the low 16 bits of the value written at 8120.
Hex 8124 is the address of the foreground color register.
Bits 31-0 are the foreground color.
DOSBox-X keeps the low 16 bits of the value written at 8124.
Hex 8128 is the address of the bitplane write mask register.
Bits 31-0 are the write mask: bit i set lets bitplane i be updated.
DOSBox-X keeps the low 16 bits of the write mask, so planes 16 to 31 cannot be enabled.
Hex 812C is the address of the bitplane read mask register.
Bits 31-0 are the read mask: bit i set makes bitplane i a data source.
DOSBox-X keeps the low 16 bits of the read mask, so planes 16 to 31 cannot be selected.
Hex 8134 and 8136 are the addresses of the background mix and the foreground mix registers.
Bits 3-0, MIX-TYPE, choose the logical operation between the new colour and the current bitmap colour.
Bits 6-5 select the colour source: background, foreground, CPU data or display memory.
Hex 8138 and 813A are the addresses of the top and left scissors; the line prints the second as R.
A write stores the top scissors limit, the lowest Y value that will be drawn.
Bits 11-0 are the clipping top limit.
A write to 813A stores the left scissors limit, the lowest X value that will be drawn.
Bits 11-0 are the clipping left limit.
Hex 813C and 813E are the addresses of the bottom and right scissors registers.
A write stores the bottom scissors limit, the highest Y value that will be drawn.
Bits 11-0 are the clipping bottom limit.
A write to 813E stores the right scissors limit, the highest X value that will be drawn.
Bits 11-0 are the clipping right limit.
Hex 8140 and 8142 are the addresses of the pixel control register and of multifunction control miscellaneous 2.
Bits 7-6 of the pixel control register select which mix register a pixel write uses.
Bits 2-0 of miscellaneous 2 are the destination base address.
Hex 8144 is the address of the multifunction control miscellaneous register and of the read register select.
Bits 1-0 of the miscellaneous register are the destination base address.
Bits 2-0 of the read register select choose which register a read of BEE8H returns.
Hex 8148 and 814A are the addresses of the minor and major axis pixel count registers.
A write stores the minor axis pixel count, the height of rectangles, image transfers, BitBLTs and PatBLTs.
Bits 11-0 are the rectangle height minus one.
A write stores the major axis pixel count, a line's length and a rectangle's width.
Bits 11-0 are the rectangle width minus one.
The streams processor registers are reached only by memory-mapped I/O, at offset 8180H for the primary stream control.
Bits 26-24, PSIDF, select the primary stream input data format, such as RGB-8 or RGB-16.
Bits 30-28, PSFC, select the primary stream filter characteristics, such as 2X stretch.
Memory offset 8184H is the colour/chroma key control register of the streams processor.
Bits 23-16, 15-8 and 7-0 are the lower bounds of the R, G and B or Y, U and V keys.
Bits 26-24, RGB CC, select how many bits of the colour are compared.
Bit 28, KC, enables colour or chroma keying outside KRGB-16.
Memory offset 8190H is the secondary stream control register; the address line prints it as S190H.
Bits 11-0 are the DDA horizontal accumulator initial value, a signed value.
Bits 26-24, SDIF, select the secondary stream input data format.
Bits 30-28, SFC, select the secondary stream filter characteristics.
A field programmed here does not take effect until the next VSYNC.
DOSBox-X stores the accumulator and the two fields at once, not at the next VSYNC.
Memory offset 8194H is the chroma key upper bound register of the streams processor.
Bits 23-16, 15-8 and 7-0 are the upper bounds of the Y, U/Cb and V/Cr keys.
Memory offset 8198H is the secondary stream stretch/filter constants register.
Bits 10-0, K1, are the initial output window width minus one.
Bits 26-16, K2, are the difference of the two window widths, a signed value.
A field programmed here does not take effect until the next VSYNC.
DOSBox-X stores both scale factors at once, not at the next VSYNC.
On a ViRGE/VX DOSBox-X takes twelve bits of each scale factor instead of eleven.
Memory offset 81A0H is the blend control register; the address line prints it as 81AOH.
Bits 4-2, Ks, are the secondary stream blend coefficient.
Bits 12-10, Kp, are the primary stream blend coefficient.
Bits 26-24, Compose Mode, select the overlay or blend of the streams, such as dissolve or fade.
A programmed field does not take effect until the next VSYNC.
DOSBox-X stores the three fields at once, not at the next VSYNC.
Memory offset 81C0H is primary stream frame buffer address 0; the title line prints it as MM81CO.
A write stores the primary stream's frame buffer starting address 0, in bits 21-0.
The address must be quadword aligned.
Memory offset 81C4H is primary stream frame buffer address 1; the title line prints it as MM81C4.
A write stores the primary stream's frame buffer starting address 1, in bits 21-0.
The address must be quadword aligned.
Memory offset 81C8H is the primary stream stride register; the title line prints it as MM81CB.
A write stores the primary stream stride, the byte offset of vertically adjacent pixels.
If double buffering is used, the stride must be the same for both buffers.
DOSBox-X keeps thirteen bits of the stride, not the twelve the document gives.
Memory offset 81CCH is the double buffer and LPB support register.
A write stores bit 0, PBS, the primary stream buffer select.
A write stores bits 2-1, SBS, which select the secondary stream buffer, alone or with an LPB input buffer.
A write stores bit 4, LIS, the LPB input buffer select.
A write stores bit 5, LSL, which the document says defers a change of bit 4 to the next end of frame.
A write stores bit 6, LST, which the document says toggles bit 4 at the end of a frame.
Memory offset 81D0H is secondary stream frame buffer address 0; the title line prints it as MM81DO.
A write stores the secondary stream's frame buffer starting address 0, in bits 21-0.
The address must be quadword aligned.
Memory offset 81D4H is secondary stream frame buffer address 1; the title line prints it as MM8104.
A write stores the secondary stream's frame buffer starting address 1, in bits 21-0.
The address must be quadword aligned.
Memory offset 81D8H is the secondary stream stride register.
A write stores the secondary stream stride, the byte offset of vertically adjacent pixels.
If double buffering is used, the stride must be the same for both buffers.
DOSBox-X keeps thirteen bits of the stride, not the twelve the document gives.
Memory offset 81DCH is the opaque overlay control register.
None of the fields have an effect unless bit 31 is set to one.
Bits 12-3 are the pixel stop fetch: a quadword offset, plus one, to the first background pixel not fetched.
Bits 28-19 are the pixel resume fetch: a quadword offset, minus one, where fetching the visible background resumes.
Bit 30, TSS, selects which stream is on top.
Bit 31, OOC, enables the opaque overlay control.
DOSBox-X takes the stop field from bits 11-0, not the document's bits 12-3.
DOSBox-X takes the resume field from bits 27-16, not the document's bits 28-19.
Memory offset 81E0H is the K1 vertical scale factor register; the address line prints it as 81EOH.
Bits 10-0, K1, are the height of the initial output window before scaling, minus one.
The value does not take effect until the next VSYNC.
DOSBox-X stores the scale factor at once, not at the next VSYNC.
Memory offset 81E4H is the K2 vertical scale factor register; the address line prints it as 81E4H.
Bits 10-0, K2, are the two's complement difference of the initial and final window heights.
The value does not take effect until the next VSYNC.
DOSBox-X stores the scale factor at once, not at the next VSYNC.
Memory offset 81E8H is the DDA vertical accumulator initial value register.
Bits 11-0 are the two's complement initial value of the vertical DDA accumulator.
The value does not take effect until the next VSYNC.
Bits 31-12 are reserved.
DOSBox-X stores the accumulator at once, not at the next VSYNC.
On a ViRGE or later DOSBox-X stores bit 15 in the EVF field.
Memory offset 81ECH is the streams FIFO and RAS controls register.
Bits 4-0 allocate the 24 FIFO slots between the primary and secondary streams.
All other allocation values are reserved and must not be programmed.
DOSBox-X splits the slots for every allocation value, including the reserved ones, subtracting 16 when above 24.
Bits 9-5 are the secondary FIFO threshold, the number of slots at which it is refilled.
Bits 14-10 are the primary FIFO threshold, the number of slots at which it is refilled.
Bit 15, RL, sets the RAS low time to 2.5 MCLKs instead of the value in CR68.
Bit 16, RP, sets the RAS pre-charge time to 1.5 MCLKs instead of the value in CR68.
Bit 18, EWS, selects one-cycle EDO memory operation for LPB memory cycles.
DOSBox-X keeps the bytes written to 8180-81FF and returns them on a read, seeding 81EC with 7000H.
Memory offset 81F0H is the primary stream window start coordinates register; the address line prints it as 81FOH.
Bits 10-0 are the screen line number plus one of the first line of the primary stream window.
Bits 26-16 are the screen pixel number plus one of the first pixel of the primary stream window.
DOSBox-X keeps ten bits of the Y start, not the eleven the document gives.
DOSBox-X keeps ten bits of the X start, not the eleven the document gives.
Memory offset 81F4H is the primary stream window size register; the address line prints it as 81F4H.
Bits 10-0 are the number of lines displayed in the primary stream window.
Bits 26-16 are the number of pixels minus one in each line of the primary stream window.
DOSBox-X keeps ten bits of the height, not the eleven the document gives.
DOSBox-X keeps ten bits of the width, not the eleven the document gives.
Memory offset 81F8H is the secondary window start coordinates register; the address line prints it as 81 F8H.
Bits 10-0 are the screen line number plus one of the first line of the secondary stream window.
Bits 26-16 are the screen pixel number plus one of the first pixel of the secondary stream window.
DOSBox-X keeps ten bits of the Y start, not the eleven the document gives.
DOSBox-X keeps ten bits of the X start, not the eleven the document gives.
Memory offset 81FCH is the secondary window size register; the address line prints it as 81FCH.
Bits 10-0 are the number of lines displayed in the secondary stream window.
Bits 26-16 are the number of pixels minus one in each line; the line names the primary window.
DOSBox-X keeps ten bits of the height, not the eleven the document gives.
DOSBox-X keeps ten bits of the width, not the eleven the document gives.
Hex 8118 is the packed MMIO address of the drawing command register, whose I/O address is 9AE8.
A read of 9AE8H returns the graphics processor status register.
Bit 9, HDW BSY, is the hardware busy flag: zero not busy, one busy executing a command.
Bit 10, AE, is set when all FIFO slots are empty.
A write of 9AE8H is the drawing command: the command and its control parameters.
Bit 0 must always be programmed to one.
Bit 1, PX MD, selects single-pixel or across-the-plane pixel transfer.
Bit 2, LAST POF, omits the last pixel of a line or vector draw.
Bit 3, DIR TYP, selects an axial or a radial drawing direction.
Bit 4, DRAW YES, selects drawing pixels or only moving the current position.
Bits 7-5, DRWG-DIR, select the drawing direction.
Bit 8, WAIT YES, makes the engine wait for data through the E2E8H port.
Bits 10-9 select the image transfer bus width: 8, 16 or 32 bits.
Bit 11 is reserved.
Bit 12, BYTE SWP, swaps the two bytes of the transfer.
Bits 15-13, CMD-TYPE, select the command: NOP, line, rectangle fill, BitBLT or PatBLT.
DOSBox-X takes bit 11 as the fourth bit of the command index, so a command with bit 11 set reaches no case and is logged as unhandled.
Every word read at 9AE8H returns AE set, but a byte read of the upper half at 9AE9H sets it only while the image transfer port waits.
Hex 8EE8 is the address of the Destination X-Position/Diagonal Step Constant register (DESTX_DIASTP).
A write is the horizontal position of the left side of the destination rectangle for BitBLTs, or the diagonal step constant for solid and textured line draws.
Bits 11-0 are the destination X-position and bits 15-12 are reserved.
Bits 13-0 are the line parameter diagonal step constant and bits 15-14 are reserved.
DOSBox-X stores bits 13-12 of the value, which the register reserves, along with the destination X-position in bits 11-0.
Hex B2E8 is the address of the color compare register (COLOR_CMP).
The register holds the color value compared against the current bitmap color when color comparison is enabled.
Bits 31-0 are the comparison color; bit 9 of BEE8_EH set makes it 32-bit, cleared two 16-bit registers, and in 32 bpp the RSF flag selects the half.
DOSBox-X keeps the colour depth's bits: 4 in 4 bpp, 8 in 8, 16 in 15/16; in 32 bpp all with control1 bit 9, else a half by bit 4.
Hex B6E8 is the address of the background mix register (BKGD_MIX) and hex BAE8 the foreground mix register (FRGD_MIX).
The mix type is one of sixteen logical operations: 0011 leaves the current color as is and 0111 writes the new color.
The BEE8H registers are written directly by writing to BEE8H with the register index in bits 15-12.
Index 0 is the minor axis pixel count: bits 11-0 are the rectangle height minus one.
Indices 1 to 4 are the top, left, bottom and right clipping limits in bits 11-0.
The power-on default of each of the four scissor registers is undefined.
Index 0Ah is the pixel control register, whose bits 7-6 select the mix register.
Index 0Dh is the multifunction control miscellaneous 2 register.
Index 0Eh is the multifunction control miscellaneous register.
Index 0Fh is the read register select register.
A read of BEE8H returns the register its read index selects, and each read increments the index.
Read index 0 to 4 returns BEE8H indices 0 to 4.
Read index 5 returns index 0A, 6 index 0E, 7 9AE8H, 8 42E8H and 9 46E8H.
Read index 0A returns index 0D, and the index increments with each read of BEE8H.
Bits 11-4 are reserved.
Bits 15-12 hold the register index 0Fh.
Read indices 5 and 6 return the pixel control and miscellaneous control registers, and 7, 8 and 9 return zero.
An index past the ten the document lists returns zero and keeps incrementing.
The dual-register helpers toggle bit 4 of control1 to choose the upper or lower word.
The setup seeds the top and left scissor limits to 0 and the bottom and right to 0FFFH.
Hex E2E8 is the write-only address of the pixel data transfer register (PIX_TRANS).
A write passes image write data from the CPU to the graphics engine in bits 15-0.
DOSBox-X clears the wait command's newline flag before drawing with the value.
On a ViRGE it also hands the value to the image transfer port when one is set.
On a 32-bit data width at 15 or 16 bpp, DOSBox-X also feeds bits 31-16 of the value unless the wait command's newline flag is set.
In the Trio64V+'s new MMIO map, offsets 100 83DO to 100 83Dx are the CRT VGA 3D? registers.
The CRT controller's index register is at 3?4H and its data register at 3?5H; a word write at 3?4H carries both.
A write to the index register loads the number of the CRT controller register to access.
A write to the data register sets the CRT controller register that the index names.
DOSBox-X ignores a third and fourth byte of a longer write to 83D4.
Hex A4D4 (BitBLT), A8D4 (2D line) and ACD4 (2D polygon) are the addresses of the source base address register (SRC_BASE).
Bits 21-3 are the source base address in video memory for 2D drawing, quadword aligned; bits 2-0 and 31-22 are reserved.
The source base is required when the source is video memory and is the 0,0 pixel address of off-screen data.
Hex A4D8 (BitBLT), A8D8 (2D line) and ACD8 (2D polygon) are the addresses of the destination base address register (DEST_BASE).
Bits 21-3 are the destination base address in video memory for 2D drawing, quadword aligned; bits 2-0 and 31-22 are reserved.
The destination base is the 0,0 pixel address of the screen resolution and normally the start of video memory.
Hex A4DC (BitBLT), A8DC (2D line) and ACDC (2D polygon) are the addresses of the left/right clipping register (CLIP_L_R).
Bits 10-0 are the right clipping limit, the last pixel drawn on each line; bits 26-16 the left limit, the first pixel; bits 15-11 and 31-27 are reserved.
Bit 1 of the Command Set register must be set for the clipping limits to have effect.
Hex A4E0 (BitBLT), A8E0 (2D line) and ACE0 (2D polygon) are the addresses of the top/bottom clipping register (CLIP_T_B).
Bits 10-0 are the bottom clipping limit, the last line drawn; bits 26-16 the top limit, the first line; bits 15-11 and 31-27 are reserved.
Bit 1 of the Command Set register must be set for the clipping limits to have effect.
Hex A4E4 (BitBLT), A8E4 (2D line) and ACE4 (2D polygon) are the addresses of the destination/source stride register (DEST_SRC_STR).
Bits 11-0 are the source stride and bits 27-16 the destination stride, their bits 2-0 zero; bits 15-12 and 31-28 are reserved.
Hex A4E8 (BitBLT) and ACE8 (2D polygon) are the addresses of the first mono pattern register (MONO_PAT_0).
Its data is used when bit 8 of the Command Set register specifies a mono pattern, and holds the pattern's first four lines.
Bits 31-0 are the low-order 32 bits of a 64-bit mono pattern; the two registers define an 8x8 pattern of line X bit Y.
Hex A4EC (BitBLT) and ACEC (2D polygon) are the addresses of the second mono pattern register (MONO_PAT_1).
Its data is used when bit 8 of the Command Set register specifies a mono pattern, and holds the pattern's second four lines.
Bits 31-0 are the high-order 32 bits of a 64-bit mono pattern; the two registers define an 8x8 pattern of line X bit Y.
Hex A4F0 (BitBLT) and ACF0 (2D polygon) are the addresses of the mono pattern background color register (PAT_BG_CLR).
The color is used for a mono pattern's zero bits when bit 8 of the Command Set register is set, its depth matching bits 4-2 of that register.
Bits 7-0 are DATA 1, bits 15-8 DATA 2 and bits 23-16 DATA 3, whose meaning depends on the colour depth; bits 31-24 are reserved.
Hex A4F4 (BitBLT), A8F4 (2D Line) and ACF4 (2D Polygon) are the addresses of the mono pattern foreground color register (PAT_FG_CLR).
It is the pattern color when Command Set bit 8 selects a mono pattern with a pattern bit of 1, and for rectangle, line and polygon fills.
The color depth must match the value selected by Command Set bits 4-2.
Bits 7-0 are DATA 1, 15-8 DATA 2 and 23-16 DATA 3, the DAC index or colour bytes by depth; bits 31-24 are reserved.
Hex A4F8 is the address of the source background color register (SRC_BG_CLR) at the BitBLT offset.
For mono image transfers (Command Set bit 6) it is the source color of an image bit of 0, and color compare (bit 9) disables it.
Bits 7-0 are DATA 1, 15-8 DATA 2 and 23-16 DATA 3, the DAC index or colour bytes by depth; bits 31-24 are reserved.
DOSBox-X keeps the value in the 2D line and polygon groups too, so a read at A8F8 returns what a write at A4F8 stored; the section names only A4F8.
Hex A4FC is the address of the source foreground color register (SRC_FG_CLR) at the BitBLT offset.
For mono image transfers (bit 6) it is the source color of an image bit of 1; with bit 9 it compares colour image data in 8 or 16 bits.
The color depth must match the value selected by Command Set bits 4-2.
Bits 7-0 are DATA 1 and 15-8 DATA 2, the DAC index or colour bytes by depth; an 8-bit color takes both bytes.
Bits 23-16 are DATA 3, reserved below 24 bits and otherwise the red index; bits 31-24 are reserved.
DOSBox-X keeps the value in the 2D line and polygon groups too, so a read at A8FC returns what a write at A4FC stored; the section names only A4FC.
Hex A504 is the address of the rectangle width/height register (RWIDTH_HEIGHT) at the BitBLT offset.
Bits 10-0 are the rectangle height in lines and bits 26-16 the width in pixels; bits 15-11 and 31-27 are reserved.
A height value of 1 equals one line and a width value of 0 equals one pixel.
DOSBox-X also accepts a write at A904 or AD04 and stores it in all three 2D groups; this section names only A504.
Hex A508 is the address of the rectangle source XY register (RSRC_XY) at the BitBLT offset.
Bits 10-0 are source Y and bits 26-16 source X, the upper left corner of the source rectangle; bits 15-11 and 31-27 are reserved.
The starting coordinate is 0,0.
DOSBox-X also accepts a write at A908 or AD08 and stores it in all three 2D groups; this section names only A508.
Hex A50C is the address of the rectangle destination XY register (RDEST_XY) at the BitBLT offset.
Bits 10-0 are destination Y and bits 26-16 destination X, of the filled rectangle or the BitBLT destination; bits 15-11 and 31-27 are reserved.
The starting coordinate is 0,0.
DOSBox-X also accepts a write at A90C or AD0C and stores it in all three 2D groups; this section names only A50C.
Hex A96C is the address of the line draw endpoints register (LXEND0_END1).
It gives the x coordinates of the first and last pixels drawn for a line, so the last pixel of a segment can be omitted for a polyline.
Bits 15-0 are END1, the last pixel x of the topmost scanline, and bits 31-16 END0, the first pixel x of the bottommost.
Bits 15-11 and 31-27 are sign bits that must be zero for a positive value.
Line draw always proceeds from bottom to top; with the last pixel withheld, an upward line takes END0 from its start x and END1 one less from its end x.
For a downward line END1 is the start x and END0 one more than the end x drawn right to left, or one less left to right.
DOSBox-X stores each 16-bit coordinate sign-extended, keeping the five sign bits the document requires to be zero.
Hex A970 is the address of the line draw X delta register (LdX).
Bits 31-0 are the X delta, minus dX shifted left 20 divided by dY with integer division, in S11.20 format with bit 31 the sign.
Hex A974 is the address of the line draw X start register (LXSTART).
Bits 31-0 are the X start in S11.20 format: x1 left-shifted 20 plus half the X delta for an X major line.
For an X major line more than one pixel may be drawn per scanline; for a Y major line at most one.
For an upward line x1 is the starting x coordinate and for a downward line the ending one.
Hex A978 is the address of the line draw Y start register (LYSTART).
Bits 10-0 are the Y start, the Y coordinate of the first scanline drawn and the largest requested y; bits 31-11 are reserved.
DOSBox-X stores 14 bits of the value, keeping bits 13-11 that the document reserves.
Hex A97C is the address of the line draw Y count register (LYCNT).
Bits 10-0 are the scan line count, the absolute difference of the end and start y plus one.
Bits 30-11 are reserved and bit 31 DIR is the direction: 0 draws right to left and 1 left to right.
DOSBox-X stores bits 13-11, which the document reserves, along with the direction bit in bit 31.
Hex AD68 is the address of the polygon right X delta register (PRDX).
Bits 31-0 are the right edge X delta, minus dX shifted left 20 divided by dY, in S11.20 format with bit 31 the sign.
Hex AD6C is the address of the polygon right X start register (PRXSTART).
Bits 31-0 are the right edge X start in S11.20: x1 left-shifted 20 minus half the delta plus 2^19 for an X major line.
For an X major line more than one pixel may be drawn per scanline; for a Y major line at most one.
For an upward line x1 is the starting x coordinate and for a downward line the ending one.
Hex AD70 is the address of the polygon left X delta register (PLDX).
Bits 31-0 are the left edge X delta, minus dX shifted left 20 divided by dY, in S11.20 format with bit 31 the sign.
Hex AD74 is the address of the polygon left X start register (PLXSTART).
Bits 31-0 are the left edge X start in S11.20: x1 left-shifted 20 minus half the delta plus 2^19 for an X major line.
For an X major line more than one pixel may be drawn per scanline; for a Y major line at most one.
For an upward line x1 is the starting x coordinate and for a downward line the ending one.
Hex AD78 is the address of the polygon Y start register (PYSTART).
Bits 10-0 are the Y start, the Y coordinate of the first scanline drawn and the largest requested y; bits 31-11 are reserved.
The value need only be programmed once for each polygon.
Hex A500 (BitBLT), A900 (2D Line) and AD00 (2D Polygon) are the addresses of the Command Set register (CMD_SET).
All registers with the same mnemonic for different commands are the same register with multiple addresses.
DOSBox-X keeps a separate Command Set register in each of the three groups, so a write at A500 does not change the value read at A900.
Bit 0 AE: 0 executes the command when this register is written; 1 executes it when the highest address register of the drawing set is written.
To turn autoexecute off without executing a command, write with bit 0 cleared and bits 30-27 set to 1111 (NOP).
Bit 1 HC enables hardware clipping; the clipping registers have effect only when it is set.
Bits 4-2 select the destination colour format: 000 8 bits per pixel palettized, 001 16 bits, 010 24 bits RGB888; others are reserved.
Bit 5 DE: 0 does not update the screen and 1 draws normally; the parameters are computed either way.
Bit 6 MS selects mono source data for image transfers, 0 meaning source data of the destination depth.
Bit 7 IDS takes source data from the image transfer port, written at 100 0000H-100 7FFFH or 100 D000H-100 EFFFH.
Bit 8 MP selects a mono pattern from the Mono Pattern registers, 0 meaning pattern data of the destination depth.
Bit 9 TP: 0 uses both source background and foreground colors for a mono image; 1 draws only where the foreground color is selected.
For a colour image transfer bit 9 compares the transmitted color with the foreground and leaves matching pixels, in 8 and 16 bits but not 24.
The transparent bit is effective only when bit 7 is set; for a mono source it gives transparent text.
DOSBox-X also honours the transparent bit in a rectangle fill, where bit 7 is not set and the document says it has no effect.
Bits 11-10 align each image transfer line: 00 byte, 01 word, 10 doubleword, 11 reserved.
With byte alignment the next line begins on the next byte of the doubleword; doubleword alignment discards the rest and word alignment uses an upper word.
Bits 13-12 are the first doubleword offset: 00 starts at the first byte, 01 the second, 10 the third, 11 the fourth.
Bits 16-14 are reserved.
Bits 24-17 are a key selecting one of 256 three-operand raster operations.
The full 256 ROPs serve BitBLT and image transfers; rectangle, line and polygon fills use only those without a source.
A pattern ROP forces the pattern value to the pattern foreground color.
Bit 25 XP: 0 performs a BitBLT from right to left and 1 from left to right.
Bit 26 YP: 0 performs a BitBLT from bottom to top and 1 from top to bottom.
Bits 30-27 select the 2D command: 0000 BitBLT, 0010 rectangle fill, 0011 line draw, 0101 polygon fill.
The other values are reserved and 1111 is NOP.
NOP is required to turn autoexecute off without executing a command.
Bit 31 23D: 0 executes a 2D command and 1 a 3D command.
Offset 859CH is the Command DMA Enable Register, read and written.
A write of bit 0 CDE: 0 disables the command DMA and 1 enables it.
Bits 31-1 are reserved.
MM850C is the Advanced Function Control Register.
Bit 0 ENB EHFC: 0 enables VGA and VESA planar modes and 1 enables all other modes, ORed with CR66 bit 0.
Bit 1 RST DM: 1 resets the read DMA pointers; software toggles it after each read DMA.
Bit 4 LA ENB: 0 disables linear addressing and 1 enables it, ORed with CR58 bit 4.
Bits 9-6, read only, count the free command FIFO slots, 0000 meaning none and 1000 eight.
Bits 3-2, bit 5 and bits 31-10 are reserved.
DOSBox-X returns bit 0 set on every read of 850CH, whatever was written.
A write stores the bit and nothing resets any read DMA pointers.
A write stores bit 4 and updates the linear framebuffer when it changes, but a read always reports bit 4 set.
Offset 8590H is the Command DMA Base Address Register, read and written.
Bit 1 BS selects a 4 KByte command buffer when 0 and 64 KBytes when 1.
Bits 31-12 are the buffer base address; bits 15-12 must be 000 for a 64K buffer.
Bit 0 and bits 11-2 are reserved.
Offset 8594H is the Command DMA Write Pointer Register, read and written.
Bits 15-2 are the write pointer: the next doubleword address after the last one written to the buffer.
Bit 16 WPU is set to 1 by software each time it updates the write pointer.
Bits 1-0 and bits 31-17 are reserved.
A write with bit 16 set also runs the command DMA immediately.
DOSBox-X keeps only bits 15-2 of the write pointer and drops bit 16, so a read never returns WPU.
Offset 8598H is the Command DMA Read Pointer Register, read and written.
Bits 15-2 are the read pointer, the address of the next doubleword the DMA reads from system memory.
The buffer address concatenates base bits 31-12 or 31-16 with the pointer, which ViRGE then updates automatically.
Bits 1-0 and bits 31-16 are reserved.
A write also clears the remaining doubleword count of the block being transferred.
Offset 8504H is the Subsystem Control Register, written only; it clears interrupt status, enables interrupts and resets the engine.
Bits 3-0 clear the vertical sync, S3d engine done, FIFO overflow and FIFO empty interrupt status.
Bits 6-4 clear the host DMA done, command DMA done and S3d FIFO empty interrupt status.
Bits 13-7 enable the host DMA done, vertical sync, engine done, FIFO overflow, FIFO empty, command DMA done and S3d FIFO empty interrupts, gated by CR32 bit 4.
Bits 15-14 S3d RST: 00 no change, 01 enables the engine, 10 resets it and 11 is reserved.
Bits 31-16 are reserved.
The write clears the status bits and stores the control value; no interrupt is enabled.
DOSBox-X keeps the written value in the chip's control member.
Only 10b resets the engine; a write stores the value and clears the status bits, so 01b leaves the engine as it is.
MM8504 is the read-only Subsystem Status Register of interrupt status, monitor I.D. and bits per pixel.
Bits 3-0 report the vertical sync, S3d engine done, FIFO overflow and FIFO empty interrupt status.
Bits 7-4 report the host DMA done, command DMA done, S3d FIFO empty and LPB interrupt status.
Bits 12-8 count the free S3d FIFO slots, 00000 meaning none and 10000 sixteen.
Bit 13 S3d ENG: 0 when the engine is busy and 1 when it is idle.
Bits 31-14 are reserved.
DOSBox-X returns the S3d FIFO empty status bit set on every read, whatever the FIFO holds.
Offset AD7CH is the Polygon Y Count Register of the polygon fill, read and written.
Bits 10-0 are the scan line count, the absolute difference of y2 and y1 plus one.
Bits 27-11 are reserved.
Bit 28 URE updates the right edge and bit 29 ULE the left edge of the polygon.
Bits 31-30 are reserved.
Table 15-1 maps the CRT VGA 3D? registers at offsets 83D0 to 83Dx.
Input Status 1 is a read-only register at 3?AH that indicates the video sync timing.
Bit 0 DTM is 0 in the display mode and 1 when either the horizontal or vertical retrace period is active.
Bit 1 is reserved as 0, bit 2 as 1, and bits 7-6 are reserved.
Bit 3 VSY is 0 in the display mode and 1 during vertical retrace.
Bits 5-4 are a video data feedback test of two color outputs selected by the AR12 plane enable register.
DOSBox-X spends CPU cycles on each read, a fraction of the maximum cycle count, and records them as removed I/O delay.
Table 15-1 places the 32K image data transfer area at offsets 0000 to 7FFF.
The image transfer area in memory is 32K, at offsets 0000H to 7FFFH.
The driver must reset the address pointer to the start before writing beyond the 32K area.
DOSBox-X also reaches the image transfer port at offsets D000 to EFFF.
When a BitBLT ROP uses a color pattern, the 8x8 pattern is stored starting at offset 100 A100H.
The space is 16, 32 or 48 doublewords at 8, 16 or 24 bits per pixel, up to A13C, A17C or A1BC.
The pattern is written from pixel 0,0 at A100 across each line, fully packed.
At 8 bits per pixel each byte is a palette index; pixel 4,0 is the low byte of A104.
At 16 bits per pixel each word is one pixel, RGB1555 or RGB565.
At 24 bits per pixel each pixel takes three bytes and the data crosses doubleword boundaries.
DOSBox-X stores the whole value in the doubleword, so a byte write replaces the other three bytes.
A word write replaces both words of the doubleword instead of updating one word.
DOSBox-X accepts offsets A1BD to A1BF and folds them into the last of the 48 doublewords.
A read of the area returns the stored pattern doubleword.
At xx = D4, Table 19-1 lists SRC_BASE for the BitBLT, 2D Line and 2D Polygon groups, each with its own address, and Z_BASE for the two 3D groups.
A read at xx = D4 returns the group's SRC_BASE.
At xx = D8, Table 19-1 lists DEST_BASE for every command group; the text calls it shared by all commands and described once with all its addresses.
A read at xx = D8 returns the group's DEST_BASE.
At xx = DC, Table 19-1's row lists CLIP_L_R five times.
A read at xx = DC returns the group's left and right clipping limits.
At xx = E0, Table 19-1's row lists CLIP_T_B five times.
A read at xx = E0 returns the group's top and bottom clipping limits.
At xx = E4, Table 19-1's row lists DEST_SRC_STR five times.
A read at xx = E4 returns the group's destination and source strides.
At xx = E8, Table 19-1 lists MONO_PAT_0 twice and Z_STRIDE twice.
A read at xx = E8 returns the group's MONO_PAT_0 register.
DOSBox-X also reads MONO_PAT_0 back at xx = E8 of the 2D Line and 2D Polygon groups, which have no such register.
At xx = EC, Table 19-1 lists MONO_PAT_1 twice and TEX_BASE once.
A read at xx = EC returns the group's MONO_PAT_1 register.
DOSBox-X also reads MONO_PAT_1 back at xx = EC of the 2D Line and 2D Polygon groups, which have no such register.
At xx = F0, Table 19-1 lists PAT_BG_CLR twice and TEX_BDR_CLR once.
A read at xx = F0 returns the group's PAT_BG_CLR register.
DOSBox-X also reads PAT_BG_CLR back at xx = F0 of the 2D Line and 2D Polygon groups, which have no such register.
At xx = F4, Table 19-1's row lists PAT_FG_CLR three times and FOG_CLR twice.
A read at xx = F4 of a 2D group returns that group's PAT_FG_CLR.
At xx = F8, Table 19-1 lists SRC_BG_CLR and COLOR0.
A read at xx = F8 returns the group's SRC_BG_CLR register.
DOSBox-X also reads SRC_BG_CLR back at xx = F8 of the 2D Line and 2D Polygon groups.
At xx = FC, Table 19-1 lists SRC_FG_CLR and COLOR1.
A read at xx = FC returns the group's SRC_FG_CLR register.
DOSBox-X also reads SRC_FG_CLR back at xx = FC of the 2D Line and 2D Polygon groups.
At xx = 100, Table 19-1's row lists Start and CMD_SET five times.
A read at xx = 100 of a 2D group returns that group's CMD_SET.
At xx = 104, Table 19-1 lists RWIDTH_HEIGHT.
A read at xx = 104 returns the group's RWIDTH_HEIGHT register.
DOSBox-X also reads RWIDTH_HEIGHT back at xx = 104 of the 2D Line and 2D Polygon groups, which the table gives no such register.
At xx = 108, Table 19-1 lists RSRC_XY.
A read at xx = 108 returns the group's RSRC_XY register.
DOSBox-X also reads RSRC_XY back at xx = 108 of the 2D Line and 2D Polygon groups, which the table gives no such register.
At xx = 10C, Table 19-1 lists RDEST_XY.
A read at xx = 10C returns the group's RDEST_XY register.
DOSBox-X also reads RDEST_XY back at xx = 10C of the 2D Line and 2D Polygon groups, which the table gives no such register.
At xx = 168, Table 19-1 lists PRdX and TdXdY01.
A read at xx = 168 returns the group's PRdX register.
At xx = 16C, Table 19-1's row lists LXEND0_END1, PRXSTART, 3XEND0_END1 and TXEND01.
A read at xx = 16C returns LXEND0_END1 of the 2D Line group and PRXSTART of the 2D Polygon group.
At xx = 170, Table 19-1's row lists LdX, PLdX, 3dX and TdXdY02.
A read at xx = 170 returns LdX of the 2D Line group and PLdX of the 2D Polygon group.
At xx = 174, Table 19-1's row lists LXSTART, PLXSTART, 3XSTART and TXSTART02.
A read at xx = 174 returns LXSTART of the 2D Line group and PLXSTART of the 2D Polygon group.
At xx = 178, Table 19-1's row lists LYSTART, PYSTART, 3YSTART and TYSTART.
A read at xx = 178 returns LYSTART of the 2D Line group and PYSTART of the 2D Polygon group.
At xx = 17C, Table 19-1's row lists LYCNT, PYCNT, 3YCNT and TY_01_Y12.
A read at xx = 17C returns LYCNT of the 2D Line group and PYCNT of the 2D Polygon group.
42E8H is the read-only Subsystem Status Register (SUBSYS_STAT) of interrupt status, monitor I.D. and bits per pixel.
A read reports the vertical sync, engine busy, FIFO overflow and FIFO empty interrupt statuses in bits 3-0 and the pixel length in bit 7; the other bits are reserved.
42E8H is also the write-only Subsystem Control Register (SUBSYS_CNTL).
Bits 3-0 clear the four interrupt statuses, bits 10-8 enable three and bit 11 the FIFO empty one; bits 7-4 and 13-12 are reserved.
Bits 15-14 GE RST: 00 leaves the engine unchanged, 01 enables it, 10 resets it and 11 is reserved.
A read at 42E8 lands in XGA_Read's default branch, which returns 0FFFFFFFFH.
A write at 42E8 feeds the image transfer port on a ViRGE card and is only logged on a Trio64V+; the interrupt statuses are not cleared.
A write at 42E8 feeds the image transfer port on a ViRGE card and is only logged on a Trio64V+; the GE RST bits are not stored.
46E8H is the Video Subsystem Enable Register, which places the Video Subsystem in setup mode; the setup text calls it read/write, its own section write only.
Bit 3 AD DEC: 0 disables and 1 enables the video I/O and memory address decoders.
Bit 4 EN SUP: 0 leaves the card in operational mode and 1 places it in setup mode.
A write at 46E8 feeds the image transfer port on a ViRGE card and is only logged on a Trio64V+; AD DEC is not stored.
A write at 46E8 feeds the image transfer port on a ViRGE card and is only logged on a Trio64V+; EN SUP is not stored.
4AE8H is the Advanced Function Control Register (ADVFUNC_CNTL), read and written.
Bit 0 ENB EHFC: 0 enables the VGA and VESA planar modes and 1 enables all the other modes.
Bit 2 ENH PL: 0 selects a 4 bits/pixel enhanced mode and 1 selects 8 or more bits/pixel, the length given by CR50 bits 5-4.
Bit 4 LA enables linear addressing and is ORed with bit 4 of CR58.
Bits 15-5 are reserved.
A write at 4AE8 feeds the image transfer port on a ViRGE card and is only logged on a Trio64V+; ENB EHFC is not stored.
A write at 4AE8 feeds the image transfer port on a ViRGE card and is only logged on a Trio64V+; ENH PL is not stored.
A write at 4AE8 feeds the image transfer port on a ViRGE card and is only logged on a Trio64V+; LA is not stored.
Hex 82E9 is the upper byte of the current V-position register (CUR_V), a 16-bit read/write register at 82E8H with position bits 11-0.
A read of the byte at 82E9 returns bits 15-8 of the current vertical drawing coordinate: position bits 11-8 and four reserved bits.
A write of the byte at 82E9 sets position bits 11-8 of the vertical coordinate; bits 15-12 are reserved.
A read at 82E9 lands in XGA_Read's default branch, which returns 0FFFFFFFFH.
A byte write at port x82E9 calls XGA_DrawWait, writes colorpat and calls S3D_Write, then logs at src/hardware/vga_xga.cpp:3019; the V-position keeps its value.
Hex 86E8H is the read/write address of the Current X-Position register (CUR_X), 16 bits wide with bits 11-0 the current X position and bits 15-12 reserved.
A read of the register's bits 15-8 returns position bits 11-8 and four reserved bits.
A write of the register's bits 15-8 sets position bits 11-8; bits 15-12 are reserved.
A byte read at port 86E9 lands in XGA_Read's default branch, whose 0FFFFFFFFH a byte access truncates to 0FFH.
A byte write at port x86E9 calls XGA_DrawWait, writes colorpat and calls S3D_Write, then logs at src/hardware/vga_xga.cpp:3019; the Current X-Position keeps its value.
Hex 8EE8H is the read/write address of the Destination X-Position/Diagonal Step Constant register (DESTX_DIASTP); bits 15-12 are reserved, and bits 15-14 when it holds the diagonal step constant.
A read of the register's bits 15-8 returns the reserved bits 15-12, or the reserved bits 15-14 when it holds the diagonal step constant, above the field's high bits.
A write of the register's bits 15-8 writes the reserved bits 15-12, or the reserved bits 15-14 when it holds the diagonal step constant, above the field's high bits.
A byte read at port 8EE9 lands in XGA_Read's default branch, whose 0FFFFFFFFH a byte access truncates to 0FFH.
A byte write at port x8EE9 calls XGA_DrawWait, writes colorpat and calls S3D_Write, then logs at src/hardware/vga_xga.cpp:3019; the Destination X-Position/Diagonal Step Constant keeps its value.
Hex 92E8H is the read/write address of the Line Error Term register (ERR_TERM), 16 bits wide with bits 13-0 the error term and bits 15-14 reserved.
A read of the register's bits 15-8 returns error term bits 13-8 and two reserved bits.
A write of the register's bits 15-8 sets error term bits 13-8; bits 15-14 are reserved.
A byte read at port 92E9 lands in XGA_Read's default branch, whose 0FFFFFFFFH a byte access truncates to 0FFH.
A byte write at port x92E9 calls XGA_DrawWait, writes colorpat and calls S3D_Write, then logs at src/hardware/vga_xga.cpp:3019; the Line Error Term keeps its value.
Hex 96E8H is the read/write address of the Major Axis Pixel Count register (MAJ_AXIS_PCNT), 16 bits wide with bits 11-0 the count and bits 15-12 reserved.
A read of the register's bits 15-8 returns count bits 11-8 and four reserved bits.
A write of the register's bits 15-8 sets count bits 11-8; bits 15-12 are reserved.
A byte read at port 96E9 lands in XGA_Read's default branch, whose 0FFFFFFFFH a byte access truncates to 0FFH.
A byte write at port x96E9 calls XGA_DrawWait, writes colorpat and calls S3D_Write, then logs at src/hardware/vga_xga.cpp:3019; the Major Axis Pixel Count keeps its value.
Hex 9EE8 is the write-only Short Stroke Vector Transfer register (SHORT_STROKE), which defines two short stroke vectors drawn one at a time.
A write sets a vector in bits 7-0: bits 3-0 the pixel length minus one, bit 4 draw or move only, and bits 7-5 the drawing direction.
A byte write at port x9EE8 calls XGA_DrawWait, writes colorpat and calls S3D_Write, then logs at src/hardware/vga_xga.cpp:3019; the Short Stroke Vector Transfer keeps its value.
The Short Stroke Vector Transfer register at 9EE8H (SHORT_STROKE) defines two vectors, one in the low byte and one in the high byte; bits 15-8 duplicate bits 7-0.
A write of the register's high byte sets the second short stroke vector the register defines.
A byte write at port x9EE9 calls XGA_DrawWait, writes colorpat and calls S3D_Write, then logs at src/hardware/vga_xga.cpp:3019; the Short Stroke Vector Transfer keeps its value.
Hex A6E8H is the read/write address of the Foreground Color register (FRGD_COLOR): bits 31-0 are the colour, in two 16-bit registers or one 32-bit register.
A read of the register's bits 15-8 returns bits 15-8 of the foreground colour.
A write of the register's bits 15-8 sets bits 15-8 of the foreground colour.
A byte read at port A6E9 lands in XGA_Read's default branch, whose 0FFFFFFFFH a byte access truncates to 0FFH.
A byte write at port xA6E9 calls XGA_DrawWait, writes colorpat and calls S3D_Write, then logs at src/hardware/vga_xga.cpp:3019; the Foreground Color keeps its value.
Hex AAE8H is the read/write address of the Bitplane Write Mask register (WRT_MASK): bits 31-0 are the mask, in two 16-bit registers or one 32-bit register.
A read of the register's bits 15-8 returns write mask bits 15-8: plane 8 to 15 is updated when its bit is one.
A write of the register's bits 15-8 sets write mask bits 15-8, one per plane 8 to 15.
A byte read at port AAE9 lands in XGA_Read's default branch, whose 0FFFFFFFFH a byte access truncates to 0FFH.
A byte write at port xAAE9 calls XGA_DrawWait, writes colorpat and calls S3D_Write, then logs at src/hardware/vga_xga.cpp:3019; the Bitplane Write Mask keeps its value.
Hex AEE8H is the read/write address of the Bitplane Read Mask register (RD_MASK): bits 31-0 are the mask, in two 16-bit registers or one 32-bit register.
A read of the register's bits 15-8 returns read mask bits 15-8: plane 8 to 15 is a data source when its bit is one.
A write of the register's bits 15-8 sets read mask bits 15-8, one per plane 8 to 15.
A byte read at port AEE9 lands in XGA_Read's default branch, whose 0FFFFFFFFH a byte access truncates to 0FFH.
A byte write at port xAEE9 calls XGA_DrawWait, writes colorpat and calls S3D_Write, then logs at src/hardware/vga_xga.cpp:3019; the Bitplane Read Mask keeps its value.
Hex B2E8H is the read/write address of the Color Compare register (COLOR_CMP): bits 31-0 are the comparison colour, in two 16-bit registers or one 32-bit register.
A read of the register's bits 15-8 returns comparison colour bits 15-8.
A write of the register's bits 15-8 sets comparison colour bits 15-8.
A byte read at port B2E9 lands in XGA_Read's default branch, whose 0FFFFFFFFH a byte access truncates to 0FFH.
A byte write at port xB2E9 calls XGA_DrawWait, writes colorpat and calls S3D_Write, then logs at src/hardware/vga_xga.cpp:3019; the Color Compare keeps its value.
Hex BEE8H is the read-only data register (RD_REG_DT); a write to BEE8H carries the register index in bits 15-12 and writes that BEE8H register.
A read of the register's bits 15-8 returns the top byte of the register that bits 2-0 of BEE8H, Index 0FH select.
A write of the register's bits 15-8 carries the register index in bits 15-12, selecting the BEE8H register written.
Writes to the BEE8H registers are pipelined, so a read-back needs a NOP drawing command written first.
A byte write at port xBEE9 calls XGA_DrawWait, writes colorpat and calls S3D_Write, then logs at src/hardware/vga_xga.cpp:3019; the BEE8h registers keep their values.
A byte read at port BEE9 lands in XGA_Read's default branch, whose 0FFFFFFFFH a byte access truncates to 0FFH.
B6E8H is the background mix and BAE8H the foreground mix register, both read/write with no defined power-on value.
Bits 15-7 of the mix registers are reserved: the document requires them written zero and leaves their read value undefined.
A write of the register's bits 15-8 writes the reserved bits as zero.
A byte write at port xBAE9 calls XGA_DrawWait, writes colorpat and calls S3D_Write, then logs at src/hardware/vga_xga.cpp:3019; the Foreground Mix keeps its value.
A byte read at port BAE9 returns 0FFH, the low byte of the 0FFFFFFFFH XGA_Read's default branch returns, where the document leaves the reserved bits' read undefined.
Hex E2EA is the write-only Pixel Data Transfer Extension register (PIX_TRANS_EXT), an extension of E2E8H for 32-bit operations.
A write carries image write data in bits 15-0.
On a ViRGE the write at E2EA feeds the image transfer port, while on a Trio64 or Trio64V+ it is only logged and stores nothing.

searched.gave: the emulator's own source header cites no document, and no comment in vga_xga.cpp names E2E0H.
S3 Graphics' site refused the connection (403); no legacy register manual could be reached there.
the Trio32/Trio64, Trio64V+ and 86C928 manuals there name the pixel transfer registers at E2E8H and E2EAH; the ViRGE book and all of them name no register at E2E0H.
the archive copies the document table lists carry the same text as the captures, and neither has a register at E2E0H.
a search for an S3 datasheet index returned the VGA Museum's manual links; none names a register at E2E0H.

rows.text: VGA_SetupXGA registers port E2E0 for XGA_Write and XGA_Read with byte, word and dword accesses.
A write at E2E0 is only logged on a Trio64 or Trio64V+, and on a ViRGE, being in D000H to EFFFH, it feeds the image transfer port.
A read at E2E0 lands in XGA_Read's default branch, which returns 0FFFFFFFFH.
